mainTopic: Acquiring land through חזקה: the seller's permission ״לך חזק וקני״, whether a gift is different, and which small acts on a fence, gap or stone count as חזקה
overview: This amud opens by finishing a ruling: if the buyer does the act of חזקה when the seller is not there, the seller must have told him ״לך חזק וקני״. רב asks whether a gift works the same way. שמואל says the answer is obvious by a קל וחומר: if a paying buyer needs permission, someone getting a gift surely does. The גמרא explains that רב was unsure because a giver gives with an עין יפה. Next, the גמרא explains the משנה's כל שהוא using שמואל's two cases: finishing a fence to ten טפחים, or widening a gap until a person can walk through. For each case it shows the small but real change involved: a fence that goes from easy to hard to climb, and a gap that goes from a squeeze to easy passage. רב אסי then quotes רבי יוחנן that placing or removing a stone that helps is a חזקה. The גמרא explains this means the stone brought water to the field, not just protected it from flooding, since saving a field is like chasing a lion off a friend's land. The amud ends with another ruling of רבי יוחנן about two fields with one boundary between them.

steps.title: When the seller is absent, he must tell the buyer to go take possession
steps.stepSummary: The ruling ends: if the act of חזקה is done when the seller is not there, the seller must say ״לך חזק וקני״.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the buyer does the act when the seller is not there, the seller has to tell him: "Go, take possession and acquire."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling that began just before this section. If the seller is not present when the buyer does the act of חזקה, the seller must clearly tell him to go take possession.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the seller watches the buyer work the land and says nothing, his silence shows he agrees. When the seller is not there, nothing shows he agrees. So he must have given clear permission ahead of time with the words ״לך חזק וקני״.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in his presence; the seller was not there
"Go, take possession and acquire"; the seller's permission for the buyer to acquire through his act
Acquiring land by doing a physical act of ownership on it

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the starting point for רב's question about gifts in the next step.

phrases.english: Not in his presence –
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started before this section. "His" means the seller.

phrases.english: he must say to him: "Go, take possession and acquire."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes a ruling that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a sale, an act of חזקה done without the seller present only works if the seller said ״לך חזק וקני״.

steps.title: רב asks how a gift is acquired
steps.stepSummary: רב asks whether a gift also needs the giver to say ״לך חזק וקני״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב asked: What about a gift? How does that work?
steps.whatsHappening: רב asks whether the rule just stated for a sale also applies to a gift. Does the person receiving a gift also need the giver to say ״לך חזק וקני״?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule above was said about a sale. רב wants to know whether a gift follows the same rule or a different one. He does not give an answer yet.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked; raised an open question

phrases.english: Rav asked:
A gift – how does it work?
phrases.notes: He means: does the receiver need to hear "Go, take possession and acquire" when the giver is not there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the sale rule from step 1 also applies to a gift.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a gift, like a sale, needs ״לך חזק וקני״ for an act of חזקה done without the giver present.

steps.title: שמואל says the answer is obvious: a gift needs it even more
steps.stepSummary: שמואל challenges the question with a קל וחומר: if a buyer who paid needs permission, someone getting a free gift surely does.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Why is אבא (רב) unsure? Think about a sale, where the buyer pays money. Even there, it only works if the seller said "Go, take possession and acquire"; otherwise it doesn't. So a gift should need it all the more!
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל does not see why רב has a question at all. He argues that the answer follows clearly from the rule about a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer has paid money, so you would expect the seller to want him to take the land. Even so, the buyer needs clear permission. Someone getting a gift paid nothing, so it is even more reasonable that he needs clear permission. This is a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: אבא, רב's personal name; שמואל uses it here
Isn't it all the more so? The wording of a קל וחומר argument

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not answering רב's question in the normal way. He is challenging it, saying the question should never have been asked because the answer is obvious.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מַאי תִּבְעֵי לֵיהּ לְאַבָּא?
phrases.english: Shmuel said: What is Abba unsure about?
phrases.notes: אבא is רב himself. שמואל is calling him by his personal name.

phrases.english: Now, if with a sale,
where he gives him money,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״לֵךְ חֲזֵק וּקְנִי״ – אִין,
phrases.english: if he said to him "Go, take possession and acquire" – yes, it works,
if not – it does not;
then with a gift, isn't it all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's question from step 2 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's question about whether a gift needs ״לך חזק וקני״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: a sale, where money was paid, still needs clear permission. A gift has no payment, so it should certainly need permission too.

steps.title: Why רב was unsure: a giver gives generously
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב's reason: someone who gives a gift gives with a generous eye, so maybe he wants the receiver to acquire even without saying so.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב thinks: someone who gives a gift gives it generously.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב still had a question. A gift may be different because the giver is being generous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל assumed a gift is weaker than a sale. רב sees a reason a gift might be stronger. The giver wants the receiver to have it with no strings attached, so maybe no clear permission is needed. This breaks the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; this is his view
A generous eye; giving willingly and openly

steps.whatToRemember: In a sale, done without the seller present, the buyer needs ״לך חזק וקני״. שמואל says a gift needs it even more. רב was unsure, because someone who gives a gift gives with an עין יפה.

phrases.english: And Rav holds:
one who gives a gift
gives it generously.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב's question against שמואל's challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a difference between the two cases that breaks the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A gift is weaker than a sale, so it surely needs ״לך חזק וקני״.
steps.terutzMaskana: A gift may be stronger in this way, because the giver gives generously. So it may work even without clear permission.

steps.title: How small is "any amount" of fencing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means when it says fencing or breaking a gap of כל שהוא counts as חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new subject. The משנה said that fencing or breaking a gap "any amount" counts as חזקה, and the גמרא asks what that really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Any amount" cannot mean a meaningless act. So the גמרא wants to know what the smallest act is that still counts as taking possession.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount, even a tiny bit

phrases.english: And how much is "any amount"?
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה, which says that putting up a fence or breaking a gap "any amount" counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, explaining a phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of the smallest fencing or gap-breaking act that counts as חזקה.

steps.title: שמואל's two examples: completing a fence or widening a gap
steps.stepSummary: Following שמואל: raising a fence to a full ten טפחים, or widening a gap until a person can go in and out, counts as חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows שמואל, who said: If someone raised a fence until it reached ten טפחים, or widened a gap until a person can go in and out through it, that counts as taking possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ruling of שמואל. He gives two examples of a small act that still counts as חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example is a small final step that creates a meaningful change. In the first, a fence that was almost there is finished to ten טפחים, the height of a proper wall. In the second, a small gap is widened until a person can walk through it. The person adds only a little, but that little makes the fence or the opening count.

keyTerms.meaning: He completed it to ten טפחים
He broke an opening in a fence

phrases.english: As in Shmuel's ruling –
for Shmuel said:
If he built up a fence and completed it to ten handbreadths,
or broke open a gap
enough that a person can go in and out through it –
this counts as taking possession.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "Any amount" means a small final addition that makes a real difference: finishing a fence to ten טפחים, or widening a gap until a person can pass through.

steps.title: Which fence case can this be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the fence example. Either the added height changed nothing, or it changed so much that it is not a "small" act.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of this fence? If people couldn't climb it before and still can't now, what did he accomplish? But if people could climb it before and can't now, he did a lot!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests שמואל's fence example by looking at two possible cases. Neither case seems to fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the extra height changed nothing, so it should not count as an act of ownership. In the second case the fence went from climbable to blocked. That is a big change, not "any amount." So the גמרא asks what case שמואל can mean.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the details?

phrases.english: This fence – what is the case?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא לָא הֲווֹ סָלְקִי לַהּ,
phrases.english: If you say that at first people could not climb over it,
and now too they cannot climb over it –
what did he accomplish?
But rather, if at first people could climb over it,
and now they cannot climb over it –
he did a lot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the fence example in step 6 fits the משנה's "any amount."
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's case of raising a fence to ten טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either the added height made no difference, so it is not an act of ownership. Or it changed the fence from climbable to blocked, which is a big act and not "any amount."

steps.title: The fence went from easy to climb to hard to climb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the case: before, people climbed the fence easily; now they can climb it only with effort. That is a real change, but a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is where at first people climbed over it easily, and now they can climb it only with difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing a middle case between the two options. Here the fence was easy to climb before and is hard to climb now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added height made a real difference, so he did something meaningful as an owner. But people can still get over the fence, so it is a small change. That fits the משנה's "any amount."

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case

steps.whatToRemember: "Any amount" in fencing means a small change that still makes a difference. One example is raising a fence so that people who used to climb over it easily can now climb it only with effort.

phrases.english: No, it is needed for this case:
where at first people climbed over it easily,
and now they climb over it only with difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא הֲווֹ סָלְקִי לַהּ בְּרַוְוחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 with a middle case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a middle case between the two options
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The added height either changed nothing or completely blocked the fence.
steps.terutzMaskana: The added height made the fence harder to climb but not impossible. That is a real change, yet small enough to be "any amount."

steps.title: What kind of gap-widening are we talking about?
steps.stepSummary: Just as it did with the fence, the גמרא challenges the gap example. Either the widening changed nothing, or it changed so much that it is not a 'small' act.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of this gap? If people could already go in through it before, and they can go in now too, what did he do? But if before people could not go in through it, and now they can, he did a lot!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same two-sided question about the gap (פרצה) that it just asked about the fence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said widening a gap even כל שהוא (a tiny bit) is a חזקה. If the gap was already usable, the widening seems to accomplish nothing. If it was not usable before and now it is, that is a big act, not a tiny one.

keyTerms.meaning: A gap or breach in a fence or wall
If you say (introduces a suggested reading the גמרא will test)
He did a lot (too much to call it 'a tiny bit')

phrases.english: This gap, what is the case?
phrases.notes: This is the gap from the משנה that he widened 'a tiny bit,' which שמואל explained in step 6.

phrases.english: If you say that at first people could go in through it,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי עָיְילִי בַּהּ – מַאי עֲבַד?
phrases.english: and now too they go in through it, what did he do?

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא לָא הֲווֹ עָיְילִי בַּהּ,
phrases.english: But rather, that at first they could not go in through it,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשְׁתָּא קָא עָיְילִי בַּהּ – טוּבָא עֲבַד!
phrases.english: and now they do go in through it, he did a lot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge of step 7, now aimed at the gap example instead of the fence example.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's explanation that widening a gap so a person can go in and out is a חזקה, and the משנה calling it 'כל שהוא'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: either no real change happened (so no חזקה), or a large change happened (so it is not 'a tiny bit').

steps.title: From squeezing through to walking in easily
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: before, people got through the gap only with difficulty; now they get through comfortably. That is a real change, but a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where at first people went in through it with difficulty, and now they go in through it with ease.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by finding a middle case, exactly like it did for the fence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gap was already passable, but only by squeezing. Widening it made passage easy. That improvement is real enough to be a חזקה, yet small enough to fit the משנה's word 'כל שהוא'.
steps.whatToRemember: For both the fence and the gap, a חזקה through a 'tiny' act means a real but small improvement: from easy to hard to climb, or from hard to easy to walk through.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where at first they went in through it with difficulty,
and now they go in through it with ease.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא הֲווֹ עָיְילִי בַּהּ בְּדוּחְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 9 by describing a middle case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a middle case between 'no change' and 'big change'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Widening a gap is either meaningless or too big to be called 'a tiny bit'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a gap that went from hard to pass through to easy to pass through: a real but small change.

steps.title: Placing or removing a stone that helps
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי quotes רבי יוחנן: if someone put down a stone or took away a stone, and it helped, that counts as a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If he put down a stone and it helped, or took away a stone and it helped, that is a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about another very small act that can count as taking ownership of a field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even moving a single stone can be a חזקה, as long as it actually helps the field. The ruling does not yet say what kind of help is meant; the גמרא will ask that next.

keyTerms.meaning: And it helped, it was useful

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he put down a stone and it helped,
or took away a stone and it helped,
this is a חזקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: נָתָן צְרוֹר וְהוֹעִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the fence and gap cases, the גמרא brings another example of a small act that counts as חזקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Placing or removing a stone in a way that helps the field is a חזקה.

steps.title: What do 'placed' and 'removed' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly רבי יוחנן meant by placing a stone and removing a stone.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'placed' mean, and what does 'removed' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear picture of the stone case. This question sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the stone 'helped' but did not say how. The גמרא wants to know what real situation he had in mind.

phrases.english: What is 'placed' and what is 'removed'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the words in רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of placing or removing a stone is meant, and how it 'helps'.

steps.title: Not protecting the field from water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the stone kept flood water out or let flood water drain away, but rejects this: that is like chasing a lion off a friend's land.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he put down a stone and blocked water from it, or took away a stone and let water out of it, this is just like chasing a lion away from a friend's property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible meaning and then pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blocking or draining flood water only saves the field from damage. Anyone would do that even for someone else's field, just like chasing off a lion, so it does not show that he is acting as the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Chasing a lion away from a friend's property: saving something from harm, which is not an owner's act

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the act is too small. The problem is that saving a field from damage is something anyone would do for another person, so it does not show ownership.

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא נָתַן צְרוֹר – וּסְכַר מַיָּא מִינַּהּ,
phrases.english: If you say he put down a stone and blocked the water from it,
phrases.notes: 'From it' means from the field: the water was flooding it.

phrases.english: or took away a stone and let the water out of it;

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַבְרִיחַ אֲרִי מִנִּכְסֵי חֲבֵרוֹ הוּא!
phrases.english: this is chasing a lion away from his friend's property!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא נָתַן צְרוֹר – וּסְכַר מַיָּא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question of step 12 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading רבי יוחנן's case as protecting the field from flood water.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Preventing damage is like chasing a lion from a friend's land: anyone would do it, so it is not an act of ownership.

steps.title: The stone brought more water to the field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes: the placed stone directed water to the field, and the removed stone increased the water flowing to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he put down a stone that brought water to it, or took away a stone and gave it more water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer to what 'placed' and 'removed' mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the stone does not save the field from harm; it improves the field by watering it. Improving land is what an owner does, so it counts as a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Joined, connected (the water to the field)

steps.whatToRemember: An act counts as חזקה when it improves the field like an owner would, not when it only protects the field from damage like any helpful neighbor would.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a clear test for חזקה: the act must show ownership, not just kindness or prevention of harm.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נָתַן צְרוֹר – דְּצַמֵּד לַהּ מַיָּא,
phrases.english: Rather, he put down a stone that brought water to it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the field: the stone turned water toward the field to water it.

phrases.english: or took away a stone and gave it more water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא נָתַן צְרוֹר – דְּצַמֵּד לַהּ מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of step 13 with the correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Placing or removing the stone improved the field's water supply, which is an owner's act.

steps.title: Two fields with one boundary between them
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי quotes another ruling of רבי יוחנן: if two fields have one boundary between them and someone did a חזקה on one of them to acquire it, he acquired it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי said that רבי יוחנן said: Two fields with one boundary between them. If he took possession of one of them in order to acquire it, he acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling from the same chain, רב אסי quoting רבי יוחנן, about acquiring fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two fields separated by a single boundary. Someone does an act of חזקה on one of them, intending to acquire it, and the ruling is that he acquires that field.

keyTerms.meaning: He did an act of taking possession

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Two fields with one boundary between them,
if he took possession of one of them to acquire it, he acquired it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁתֵּי שָׂדוֹת וּמֶצֶר אֶחָד בֵּינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling from the same speakers as step 11, on a related topic of acquiring fields.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two fields share one boundary, a חזקה done on one of them with intent to acquire it acquires that field.
